A moody but realistic city photograph at dusk under low cloud: A tall slim LED screen tower stands in a shallow reflecting pool on a city plaza at dusk while the skyscrapers behind dissolve into low cloud.

References: Image 1 is THE REFERENCE SCENE: recreate this place, camera, weather, light and mood closely; the tower screen becomes plain white with nothing on it. Image 2 is THE LOOK REFERENCE: take only its light, colour, grade, grain, weather and mood; ignore its subject, layout and the content of any screen. The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera from across the plaza at the height of the tower middle, 85mm lens, f/2.8, verticals parallel. The tower stands on the centre line, its screen filling about 70 percent of the frame height, sharp; its light lies as a long column on the wet stone and water below; skyscrapers to both sides fade up into grey cloud, their windows faint. The mist and cloud stay far behind the design surface: it is crisp and clear, with nothing soft, hazy or glowing over its face or edges. A few tiny figures in dark coats stand or pass far below it, small dark shapes; no face shows.

Place: A real city at dusk under heavy low cloud: the tops of towers disappear into grey cloud, mist sits in the middle distance, streets and stone are wet; small warm windows and street lights far off.

Light: Last blue-grey dusk light under heavy cloud, quite dark; the screen or billboard is the brightest thing in the frame and lights the wet ground near it; city lights small and soft in the distance.

Palette and grade: The same grade on every image: muted desaturated greys and charcoal, a slight cool tint in the cloud, small warm sodium lights, deep but not crushed shadows; the design surface pure neutral white.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph in a real city, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, never a tiny screen in a wide view. It is an unstaged photograph of a real place on a real day, with small honest signs of weather and age on the place only; the design surface itself is new and clean. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. Exposure is honest, but the design surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation or bloom around lights.

Design surface: THE TOWER SCREEN SHOWS A PLAIN WHITE FULL-SCREEN IMAGE, glowing bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, evenly lit edge to edge yet not blown out, with crisp corners meeting its thin black frame; nothing crosses it.

Finish: Shot on 35mm Kodak Portra 800 pushed one stop in low light: visible natural grain, muted soft film colour, slight lens falloff, honest underexposed dusk. Moody but believable, like a real photograph from a real evening; never a render, never cinematic teal and orange.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, mist, haze or glow over or around the design surface, any object not named in the shot, a teal and orange grade, a clean smooth digital look.
